catalog_policy: Mappings from evidence questions to presentation views. Required tokens check declared field presence, not scientific truth, visible placement, or statistical validity. Source traces are separately required by the visual-plan validator.
uncertainty_policy: Use only supplied or reproducibly verified uncertainty. Identify independent unit and sample/run context; when uncertainty is unavailable, label that limitation rather than inventing intervals.

recommended: Labeled dot plot with supported error bars when available.
Bars for magnitude with a zero origin, or a compact table when exact values are central.
avoid: Decorative depth or area that changes apparent magnitude.
Unlabeled metric direction, altered method order, or a hidden truncated axis.
A superiority title unsupported by the scope and uncertainty of the measurements.
accessibility: Directly label methods and values needed for the claim.
Use markers or patterns as well as color.
Describe the comparison and its limitation in alternative text or accessible companion text.
review_context: Identify dataset/population, evaluation protocol, independent unit, sample/run count where available, and uncertainty status.
The four required tokens preserve caller compatibility; they do not waive the context review.

recommended: Observed points at their actual positions, with lines only when the order has meaning.
Labeled small multiples when several series cannot be read in one view.
avoid: Connecting missing observations as if measured.
Mixing elapsed time, iterations, and samples without identifying the axis.
Using a smoothed curve without showing or explaining the underlying observations.
accessibility: Label each series or pair a legend with distinct line styles.
State the observed trend and material gaps in the description.
Provide the underlying values or an accessible summary when needed.

recommended: Individual observations when their number permits inspection.
Histogram or summary distribution plot with its binning or summary definition stated.
avoid: A mean-only view when dispersion is the question.
Comparing groups with unexplained changes in bin width or normalization.
Treating repeated measurements as independent samples.
accessibility: Label groups and summarize center, spread, and relevant outliers in text.
Use shapes or patterns alongside grouping colors.
Explain the meaning of box, whisker, or density marks.

recommended: Scatter plot with labeled axes and documented pairing.
A fitted relationship only when its model and uncertainty are supplied.
avoid: A causal title supported only by correlation.
Hiding overlapping points or unexplained excluded observations.
Displaying a fitted line as raw observation.
accessibility: Describe the association, grouping, and unusual points without relying on position alone.
Use distinct markers and labels for groups.
Supply a numeric summary or data reference for precise inspection.

recommended: Matched condition table with the common reference retained.
Paired differences or points when the measurements support that pairing.
avoid: Attributing a change to one component when other conditions changed.
Dropping the reference condition or unfavorable variants.
Treating unreported uncertainty as zero.
accessibility: Write component states explicitly, including absent or disabled states.
Use text labels for positive, negative, and inconclusive differences.
Describe the measured effect and the limits of the interpretation.

recommended: Point estimate and labeled interval with a common scale.
Individual runs beside the aggregate when available and relevant.
avoid: Invented error bars for single values.
Unlabeled mixing of standard deviation, standard error, confidence intervals, and ranges.
A significance conclusion inferred only from visual interval overlap.
accessibility: State what the interval encodes and its level where applicable.
Use endpoint or estimate labels when exact values matter.
Provide an accessible numeric account of estimates and intervals.

recommended: Heat map with a labeled scale and defined coordinates or cell meanings.
Small multiples with a shared scale for comparable conditions.
avoid: Unexplained per-panel normalization.
Using a color scale as evidence of physical units when the data are normalized intensities.
Rendering missing values as ordinary low values.
accessibility: Label values or key regions needed for the claim.
Describe the spatial or matrix pattern and any missing cells.
Provide a table or textual summary where color differences carry essential values.

recommended: Matched sample rows with method columns and consistent crop markers.
A full context frame beside an explicitly located enlargement.
avoid: Different crop, range, or aspect ratio presented as a direct comparison.
Examples selected for appearance without a selection note.
Claims about physical accuracy from appearance alone.
accessibility: Label every sample and method outside the image.
Describe the relevant visible difference and its limits.
Use crop markers and text to identify regions rather than color alone.

recommended: Labeled stacked bars when comparing proportions across groups.
A compact table when denominator and exact shares need close inspection.
avoid: Percentages with different or unstated denominators.
Treating overlapping categories as a partition of one whole.
Unexplained normalization of incomplete totals.
accessibility: Label categories and their shares directly when practical.
Pair color with labels or patterns.
State the denominator and any excluded or missing category in text.

recommended: Dated milestones with explicit observed or planned state.
Dependency view when ordering and blockers matter more than elapsed duration.
avoid: Presenting target dates as completion evidence.
Unmeasured percentage completion or implied certainty of future delivery.
Hiding a dependency to simplify the visual.
accessibility: Write status words beside each milestone.
Use shapes or connector labels to distinguish dependencies and states.
Provide a linear text account of actions, dates, and unresolved blockers.
